title: 2025-04-11 Redwood discovery Acme Retail AI - latency & throughput
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency needs, streaming behavior, and token/sec benchmarking for Acme's shopping assistant. AE/SE clarified current traffic patterns, sequence lengths, acceptable SLOs, and deployment preferences (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Next steps: send security pack, share benchmarking guide, run a short hosted pilot with targeted p95 tests and follow-up technical deep dive to scope Dedicated sizing.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
action_items: Jordan Lee: send pricing + Dedicated sizing worksheet (due: 2025-04-15)
Maya Patel: share benchmarking guide and sample load script (due: 2025-04-14)
Priya Menon: provide sample prompt distributions and peak concurrency window (due: 2025-04-13)
Sam Rodriguez: confirm internal decision timeline and stakeholders for Dedicated (due: 2025-04-20)
next_steps: Redwood to run a 24-hour hosted pilot with p95 telemetry for Acme's typical prompts
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) to go through networking and Private deployment constraints
Share SOC2/ISO pack and VPC/on-prem checklist
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood AE. quick round robin?
[00:07] Sam Rodriguez: Sam here CTO, Priya is with me, and Liam and Anita.
[00:12] Priya Menon: hi all.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: Awesome thanks. Maya from our side is the SE, she'll dig into latency numbers and benchmarks. Maya?
[00:22] Maya Patel: hi, thanks. quick agenda — p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, tokens/sec expectations, then tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[00:31] Sam Rodriguez: sounds good. our use case is a shopping assistant — very latency sensitive for live chat and voice. target p95 in UI is sub 500ms for short replies, 1s for richer multi-sentence answers. concurrency during peak holiday spikes maybe 1k concurrent sessions, sustained 300 during normal peak.
[00:48] Jordan Lee: great, that helps. are you currently running anything in prod?
[00:52] Sam Rodriguez: we have an inference cluster on-prem for older models, but it's very variable. we do some batch for recommendations. most real-time is handled by a 3rd party API but cost is exploding.
[01:02] Priya Menon: also want streaming for voice tokens; tokenization and chunk latency matter.
[01:07] Maya Patel: when you say streaming, do you mean server-sent events with token-by-token, or chunked streaming where you buffer small groups of tokens?
[01:13] Priya Menon: token-by-token is ideal for voice TTS latency, but chunked 50-100 token groups is acceptable if it meaningfully reduces p95.
[01:21] Jordan Lee: noted. what's your typical prompt and completion lengths?
[01:24] Priya Menon: prompts average 80-120 tokens, completions 40-150 tokens depending on the flow. the voice use-case tends to have shorter completions but we need sub-200ms first token ideally.
[01:35] Maya Patel: that's helpful. two axes to consider: per-request latency (p95) and overall throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec at concurrency). For Hosted we can often get predictable p95 for short sequences via warm pools and autoscaling; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and more predictable tail latency. Private on-prem gives full control but you manage networking, warm-starts, and kernel selection.
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: what's the typical tokens/sec per GPU we should expect?
[01:59] Maya Patel: it depends on model size and quantization. as rule of thumb: for a 13B quantized model on A100-ish class we typically see 2000-6000 tokens/sec per GPU for sampling workloads, but that number drops when you have high concurrency and small sequence lengths due to context switching and batching inefficiencies. For low latency single-threaded streaming, effective tokens/sec can be lower — maybe 500-1500 depending on beam/sample config.
[02:22] Sam Rodriguez: those are broad ranges — can Redwood run benchmarks with our actual prompt corpus?
[02:26] Jordan Lee: yes, we run benchmark pilots. Maya will outline the benchmark guide and we'll set up a hosted run first.
[02:31] Maya Patel: benchmark approach: 1) run p95 latency tests at target concurrency using your distribution of prompt/completion lengths; 2) test streaming (token-by-token + chunked); 3) measure tokens/sec per instance and overall throughput; 4) exercise cold-start and scale-up scenarios. we provide sample load scripts (locust/gatling) and a small harness to capture token-level timings.
[02:50] Priya Menon: do you measure prefix/KV cache hit behavior? our flows reuse user context a lot so cache is important.
[02:55] Maya Patel: yes we can include prefix/KV cache experiments. caching can reduce p95 by avoiding re-encoding long prefixes and by keeping KV cache warm for tiled requests; it does complicate batching.
[03:05] Anita Shah: curious tradeoffs — if we need p95 < 300ms for short answers, is Hosted realistic or do we need Dedicated?
[03:11] Maya Patel: Hosted can hit p95 < 300ms for very short sequences if you size warm pools and use streaming optimizations, but guarantees at scale are easier on Dedicated because you reserve GPU pools and avoid noisy neighbors. Also with Dedicated you can apply lower-level runtime tweaks and kernel selections.
[03:27] Jordan Lee: also routing policies — we can route high-QPS, low-latency traffic to Dedicated or warm-backed nodes and route less sensitive workloads to cheaper variants.
[03:36] Sam Rodriguez: what's the network overhead for Private — our infra team worries about VPC egress, NAT latency, and internal load balancers.
[03:42] Maya Patel: Private (VPC/on-prem) places the runtime in your network — network hops are within your environment so you often have lower observed RTTs to your app, but you need to account for model loading times, hardware availability, and OS/kernel tuning. We'll share an on-prem checklist (NIC tuning, NUMA, batch size recommendations).
[03:59] Priya Menon: tokenization differences between models can affect tokens/sec. do you provide tokenizers/exact byte-pair settings to align metrics?
[04:06] Maya Patel: yes our benchmark harness uses the exact tokenizer used by the model to ensure token counts align. we'll ask you to provide sample prompts so we test with identical tokenization.
[04:15] Jordan Lee: any security blockers — Sam?
[04:18] Sam Rodriguez: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML enterprise SSO, KMS for key management for Private. logging/audit access is important.
[04:25] Jordan Lee: we have SOC2 docs and KMS integrations; we'll send the security pack and a VPC/KMS runbook.
[04:30] Maya Patel: back to benchmarking — small note: streaming single-token latencies are dominated by scheduling and RPC overhead; one optimization is to aggregate small tokens into micro-batches (e.g., 5-10 tokens) for tradeoff between first-token latency and throughput. we'll show the trade curves.
[04:47] Priya Menon: for voice first token is critical — can you prioritize that path?
[04:50] Maya Patel: yes we can prioritize a 'fast-path' for first-token where we disable large batching and keep a warm reserved token processing lane. it's more expensive but reduces p95.
[04:59] Liam O'Connor: for Dedicated sizing how do you translate concurrency to number of GPUs?
[05:02] Maya Patel: we build a model: take average tokens/sec per GPU for your prompts, factor in concurrency and required p95 headroom, then add buffer for autoscaling and burst. For example, if you need sustained 300 concurrent sessions with average 50 tokens per response and average 5 tokens/sec per session, that's 1500 tokens/sec sustained; if a GPU can sustain ~3000 tokens/sec for that workload, you'd start with 1 GPU for baseline but then add more for p95 headroom and redundancy — we typically recommend at least N+1 for failover. We'll run actual sims with your data.
[05:30] Jordan Lee: also note quantization: int8/int4 helps throughput but sometimes increases per-token CPU overhead in pre/post processing; we'll include quantized variant tests.
[05:39] Sam Rodriguez: what about fallback policies? if Dedicated is overloaded can requests route to Hosted?
[05:43] Jordan Lee: yes smart routing supports policy-based fallbacks — you can route to Hosted variants or cheaper models when Dedicated is saturated. that's part of our unified runtime.
[05:51] Priya Menon: logging and tracing — we need per-token tracing to debug latency spikes. is that available?
[05:56] Maya Patel: we provide per-request and per-token timing hooks, and can surface p50/p95/p99 in Console. for pilot we'll enable verbose traces for a short window.
[06:05] Anita Shah: cost — what's the unit economics when you push for lower p95?
[06:09] Jordan Lee: lower p95 often means reserved capacity or more GPUs (higher cost), and streaming micro-batches reduce batching efficiency (more cost). Redwood Optimize recommendations will show tradeoffs and cost delta for configurations.
[06:20] Sam Rodriguez: timeline — we want a pilot next week if possible. tech decision by end of month.
[06:24] Jordan Lee: we can start a 24-hour hosted pilot with the harness this week. we'll need your prompt set and peak concurrency window.
[06:30] Priya Menon: i'll share prompts and token distribution by EOD tomorrow.
[06:33] Maya Patel: i'll share the load script and instructions. we'll run p95 collection and also provide token/sec heatmaps.
[06:40] Jordan Lee: perfect. any final questions?
[06:43] Sam Rodriguez: curious if you can do A/B between quantized and FP16 for p95 delta.
[06:47] Maya Patel: yes we can include that in the pilot.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: ok let's recap next steps — Jordan to send pricing and Dedicated worksheet, Maya to send benchmark guide and load scripts, Acme to send prompt corpus and concurrency windows, Redwood to run 24h hosted pilot and follow up with technical deep dive.
[06:58] Sam Rodriguez: sounds good thanks everyone.
[07:01] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the docs and schedule.
notes: Mentions of specific hardware and numbers are approximate; transcript contains typical ASR errors and casual speech patterns.
